judgment.rationale: Both Content SFIs sit under Competency C-2.3 (CG-2) and address estimating sums and differences by rounding. This is substantive extension to larger place values rather than generic repetition, and fluency with nearest-10 estimation supports success with the broader Class-5 range, so the lower-rank Class-4 Content builds towards the higher-rank Class-5 Content (second_to_first). judgment.rationale: Both are Class-4 Content bullets (equal canonical rank 3) under Competency C-2.5 ('Identifies, describes and extends simple number patterns'). The first, 'Order of numbers in multiplication', is elaborated by its LC as recognising that changing the order of factors does not change the product (commutativity); the second, 'Patterns in division (9÷3, 90÷3, 900÷3, 9000÷3)', is elaborated as identifying and extending division patterns involving multiples of ten (place-value structure). These are complementary explorations of structural patterns in the multiplication/division operations within one competency, reinforcing the same pattern-seeking skill on related inverse operations, but neither content statement's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other: commutativity of multiplication is not a stated basis for place-value division patterns, and same-rank placement provides no directional evidence. Token/trigram and page-proximity signals are weak ('in', 'of') and are not treated as semantic support. Endpoint source evidence is truncated and ancestors carry merge context, limiting deeper interpretation, so the symmetric relation is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Competency C-3.1 (attributes of 2D/3D shapes) and Curricular Goal CG-3. The Class-3 item (rank 2) is 'Models objects using these shapes', with LC 'Model objects using 2D and 3D shapes' — hands-on construction/modelling that establishes familiarity with solids such as cubes and their faces/edges. The Class-4 item (rank 3) is 'Drawing cubes on a triangular dot paper', LC 'Draw cubes on triangular dot paper' — a more demanding representational task requiring the learner to depict a three-dimensional solid on a two-dimensional isometric grid. Concrete modelling of 3D shapes plausibly supports success at representing a cube pictorially, and the coordinate order is lower-to-higher (Class-3 → Class-4), so the permitted direction is first_to_second. Both operationalise the same competency C-2.3 (relationships among operations, applying the four operations), and pattern recognition in operations meaningfully reinforces the place-value/partial-product regularities used in multi-digit multiplication, giving substantive topical coherence. However, the evidence does not show that pattern identification is an extension, deepening or enabling precursor of this particular multiplication computation content: the Class-4 bullet is generic and its shared signals with the Class-5 bullet are only weak (single shared LC token "four", trigram overlap of common suffixes, same-page proximity, shared parent), so the stronger Class-4 -> Class-5 buildsTowards claim is not supported. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-3 (rank 2) Content bullets under the same Competency C-4.2 / Curricular Goal CG-4 on selecting suitable units and tools for measuring attributes. The first covers weight (kilogram, more than/less than 1 kilogram, simple balance); the second covers length (metre, half and quarter metre, more than/less than 1 metre, measuring tape). Their Learning Components show parallel skills — measuring in a standard unit with an appropriate tool and comparing objects against one unit — applied to two different measurable attributes. Same-rank developmental direction lacks substantive supporting evidence, so the symmetric relation is appropriate. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-5 Content bullets (same rank 4) under Competency C-2.3 / CG-2.
